newsitem.title: USA: Mellon to buy pension money management firm.
newsitem.headline: Mellon to buy pension money management firm.

text.p: Mellon Bank Corp. said Monday it agreed to buy Buck Consultants Inc., a New York-based consulting firm that provides administrative and consulting services for corporate pension and benefit plans with more than $400 billion in assets.
Under the agreement, the privately held Buck will become a Mellon subsidiary and keep its current management team, Mellon said.
Mellon's stock was up 37.5 cents at $74.25 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Buck provides a broad array of pension and health and welfare actuarial services, and employee benefits, compensation and human resources consulting and administrative services to approximately 5,000 clients, ranging from small businesses to large, multinational corporations.
The firm has 65 offices in 16 countries and serves pension and other benefit plans covering more than 10 million active and retired employees.
Joseph LoCicero, president and chief executive officer of Buck, will become a member of Mellon's senior management committee.

"Merging with Mellon gives Buck the opportunity to leapfrog our competition," said LoCicero. "Together, we have vast resources, leading-edge systems and technology, and the ability to deliver an integrated array of benefits-related services to the clients of both companies."
Mellon Vice Chairman W. Keith Smith said, "Combined, we will be able to provide a full range of consulting and benefits outsourcing services to our clients that is unmatched in the industry."
Founded in 1916, Buck is the oldest pension and health and welfare actuarial, and employee benefits and compensation consulting firm in North America.
Buck reported total revenues of $197 million for the fiscal year ended March 31, of which $50 million was generated by non-U.S. operations.
Mellon expects to retain substantially all Buck employees following completion of the acquisition, and to add to total employment as the growth of the combined companies accelerates.
Buck is the seventh largest benefits consultant in the United States and the eighth largest in the world based on U.S. and worldwide benefits consulting revenues.
